I get it, but you really don't have to worry. Once the fermentation gets going it kills any pathogens that might be there, its just important not to let fresh air into contact with the kimchi by keeping it submerged in its juices. Also sterilize jars and utensils with boiling water beforehand.

There's ton of guides but the gist of it is to wash and chop up napa cabbage, salt it really generously (like half a cup of salt per head of cabbage) add water if necessary (it seeps juices on its own) to make brine and let it soak for a while (few hours or overnight). You then squeeze out remaining juices, the resulting cabbage looks really wilted as it loses most of its moisture. Wash it several times with clean water to get the excess saltiness out and pack it tightly into a jar. Weight it down with something food safe like a small bowl or plate or something, I always put water filled ziplock bag on top of it to help get a good seal and weight it down more. Keep it at room temperature for a few days to get the fermentation going, it starts smelling like cabbage-garlic farts and then transfer it into a fridge.

Now obviously to make proper kimchi you add other vegetables like carrots, onion, tons of garlic, grated ginger, alot of chilli flakes etc., but its not strictly necessary. You can ferment pretty much everything like this. To make sauerkraut you use finely grated white cabbage and add lots of caraway seeds.
